newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wise men see '97 deficit 3.3 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: German wise men see '97 deficit 3.3 pct of GDP.

text.p: Germany's budget deficit will miss Maastricht targets next year, falling only to 3.3 percent of gross domestic product from 4.2 percent this year, Handelsblatt on Thursday quoted a report by an independent panel saying.
The report, by the five "wise men" group of government economic advisers, also sees the economy growing by 2.5 percent after expanding by 1.5 percent this year.
German Finance Minister has vowed in the face of widespread criticism to bring the deficit below the three percent limit required to qualify for European economic and monetary union.
Details of the report were published in German newspapers ahead of its official release on Friday, but could not be immediately confirmed at the Economics Ministry.
The Bild newspaper said earlier that the report also forecast unemployment rising to 4.1 million from 3.9 million this year, while inflation would remain low at 1.75 percent in 1997.
